$description: Fire's export rules as data: how one piece of Fire markup is written in Lit, React/Next.js and Vue so that it renders the same DOM. spec/EXPORT.md is the prose form; every rule here carries the id of its row there (A1, F3, M2, …). An exporter reads this file; it never guesses a rule that is not here.

schema.version: Integer. Bumped when a key changes meaning.
schema.fire: The Fire version these rules describe.
schema.targets: Target id → { name, versions: { package: exact version the rules were verified against }, notes }. Target ids: html, lit, react, vue. React rules also cover Next.js (App Router).
schema.verification: Experiment id → what was run. Every rule's `check` lists experiment ids, 'R' (read from source) or 'A' (assumption the starters must prove).
schema.placeholders: Names used inside templates: {name} attribute name, {value} literal string value, {expr} an expression in the target's language, {cond} a boolean expression, {json} an expression giving JSON text, {event} an fd:* event name, {handler} a function expression, {ref} a React ref, {children} rendered children, {list} a list expression, {as} the loop variable, {tag} an element name, {key} a key expression.
schema.helpers: Functions the exporter writes once per export into `fire-export.(js|ts)` and imports where a template names them. Value: name → { source, use }.

attributes.rename: target → { html attribute name → name to write }. Applies on HTML and SVG elements; not on custom elements (see customElementNames).
attributes.customElementNames: target → rule for attribute names on custom elements (fd-*, any tag with a hyphen).
attributes.htmlBooleans: HTML boolean attributes (their presence is the value). Per target, `present` is how a present boolean is written statically, `bound` how a state-dependent one is written. React's prop name comes from rename.
attributes.presence: Attributes Fire uses by presence alone (written with no value, value ""): any data-* or aria-* written with no value, plus `popover`. `present` and `bound` per target.
attributes.string: Attributes with a string value: static and bound templates per target.
attributes.optional: An attribute that may be absent: bound template per target that drops it for undefined/null.
attributes.enumeratedNotBoolean: Attributes React does not treat as boolean although HTML allows them bare; write the value explicitly.
attributes.forbidden: Attributes and constructs never written in any target, with the reason.

schema.text: Text and whitespace rules: id → { rule, perTarget, check }.
schema.fields: Form fields not controlled by the framework: id → { markup, lit, react, vue, check }.
schema.specialElements: Elements frameworks treat specially: id → { match (CSS selector or description), lit, react, vue, why, check }.
schema.svg: SVG rules: React renames are in attributes.rename.react; this lists the remaining rules.
schema.icons: The icon rule: what is forbidden, the element form, the exact static SVG form (a template with {name}, {size}, {class}, {rest}), the sprite.
schema.customElements: Fire's custom elements: registration, attributes vs properties per target, typing, compiler options.
schema.events: fd:* events: names, binding templates per target, what does not work.
schema.lifecycle: When init(root) runs: id → { when, lit, react, vue, check }.

ownership.fireOwnedAttributes: Attributes Fire writes after init; frameworks write their first value only and never bind them to changing state.
ownership.fireOwnedAttributePatterns: Regular expressions for Fire-owned attribute names.
ownership.filledContainers: Components whose children Fire inserts, replaces or moves: { selector, fire (what Fire does), rule (what the framework does), check }.
ownership.fireWrittenFields: Fields whose value or checked state Fire writes: never controlled in React; prefer fd:change over v-model in Vue.

schema.next: Next.js server rendering and hydration rules: id → { rule, check }, plus `layout` and `runtime` code templates.
schema.csp: Strict Content Security Policy per target.
schema.facet: Facet board constructs → per-target templates. `confirm: true` marks shapes to confirm with the Facet session.
schema.renderEqual: Normalisations render-equal must apply for these rules to hold: id → description.
schema.pages: Page-level rules added in 0.8 (EXPORT.md section 17): id → { rule, lit, react, vue, check }.

html.name: Plain HTML
html.notes: Fire markup as in docs/ and templates/.

react.name: React and Next.js
react.notes: Next.js App Router with Turbopack; JSX compiled by SWC in Next, which rejects namespaced attribute names.

vue.name: Vue
vue.notes: Single-file components, single-page app; server rendering (Nuxt) is out of scope.

verification.E1: React: 72 markup cases, renderToStaticMarkup and createRoot (development build) in Chromium; DOM, property probes and warnings compared.
verification.E2: React: 42 HTML and 40 SVG attribute renames rendered on the server without warnings.
verification.E3: React: renderToString then hydrateRoot with Fire's boot.js and fire.js, 9 orders; hydration and recoverable errors recorded.
verification.E4: React: Fire changes the DOM, then React re-renders (drawn icon, secret, tabs, keyed remount, growing list).
verification.E5: React controlled input and Vue v-model against a value set in code followed by an input event.
verification.E6: Vue: 47 single-file components built with Vite (production, whitespace preserve, no isCustomElement) and run in Chromium; same templates through @vue/server-renderer.
verification.E7: Vue: v-fire directive (mounted, updated) with Fire's modules; re-render, v-if removal, keyed remount.
verification.E8: Lit: 22 template cases with render() (development build) and Fire alongside (menu state, icons, events).
verification.E9: Next.js 16.4.6: production build and development server; proxy.ts nonce CSP, boot.js in head, Fire loaded in a client effect, re-init after route change, hydration warnings with and without suppressHydrationWarning, namespaced JSX under SWC.
verification.E10: Strict policy script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' on the Vue production build and on the Lit page with Fire running: no violations.
verification.E11: A sprite marked hidden and <use> references to it render in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
verification.E12: Vue compileTemplate output: $index as a v-for alias stays local; @fd:select compiles to the key "onFd:select".
verification.R: Read from Fire's source (fire/js) or Facet's (vendor/facet/src), not run.

jsonForScript.use: Text of every <script type="application/json"> the exporter writes (M2, N5).

ccAttr.source: export const ccAttr = (v) => (v === false || v == null ? undefined : v === true ? '' : String(v));

ccText.source: export const ccText = (v) => (v == null || typeof v === 'boolean' ? '' : String(v));

ccTruthy.use: Facet cc-if (B2) and boolean live properties (B6).

notes.react: rowSpan only on td/th (React drops it elsewhere). Prefer href over xlink:href on <use>.

customElementNames.react: as in HTML; className and class both write class; htmlFor is NOT mapped (it writes htmlfor), so write for. Data goes through properties (customElements.properties).

never.react: {name}="" (React reads an empty string as false and drops the attribute)

fieldStateOverrides.autofocus: A3 (React writes no attribute on the client; render-equal R6)

presence.match: data-* or aria-* written with no value or value "" in Fire markup, and popover written bare

string.booleanValues: aria-* with a boolean expression: all targets write "true"/"false" (React and Vue convert; in Lit write String({expr})).

optional.why: Lit renders undefined and null as an empty attribute; React and Vue drop the attribute for undefined and null.

popover.react: popover="" or popover="auto" | "manual"; React drops popover={true}

forbidden.what: style attribute, JSX style={…}, Vue :style, Vue v-show (writes style="display: none"), Lit styleMap
forbidden.instead: data-fd-vars for custom properties; hidden or v-if for visibility

forbidden.what: <i data-icon> in Lit, React or Vue code

T1.rule: Whitespace containing a newline between inline elements renders as one space in HTML.
T1.react: write {' '} where the HTML has it

T3.rule: Named entities (  → &) are the same text in every target.

T4.rule: HTML comments: kept by Lit, dropped by JSX and by Vue production builds; render-equal ignores them.

T5.rule: Text from a value: Lit and Vue print booleans as words, React prints nothing; null and undefined print nothing everywhere. Facet holes go through ccText.

F3.react: <select defaultValue="b"> (array when multiple); no selected on <option>
F3.vue: selected on the option, or :selected="{cond}"; never :value on <select>

F7.why: React's onChange ignores a value Fire sets in code and later restores its own; Vue v-model follows the input event Fire sends.

M1.lit: static content in html`` is fine; with data: <template {attrs} .innerHTML=${{json}}></template>; no expressions inside
M1.why: Framework-rendered children go to childNodes, not .content.

M2.why: React children text with </script breaks hydration; Vue drops <script> from templates (production) or fails the build (development).

M3.react: in the root layout <head>, data-fd-labels="" and dangerouslySetInnerHTML

M4.rule: never write or bind open; open with overlays.openDialog(ref) or [data-fd-dialog-open]

M5.rule: open only as the start value; Fire writes open and data-state; listen for fd:change

M7.why: Fire wraps a bare table with replaceWith; the framework then loses the table's parent.

M8.rule: write <div class="fd-doc-table" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="{caption or Table}"> around it

M9.match: a submenu .fd-menu opened from a menu item
M9.why: Fire moves it there with append

S1.rule: viewBox, d, x, y, width, height, fill, stroke, aria-hidden, data-* unchanged in every target

S2.rule: hyphenated presentation attributes: camelCase in React (attributes.rename.react), unchanged elsewhere

S3.rule: <use href="#id"> unchanged; prefer href to xlink:href

S5.rule: Lit: <svg> inside html`` gets the SVG namespace from the HTML parser; the svg tag function is not needed

icons.forbidden: i[data-icon] in Lit, React and Vue code
icons.why: Fire replaces the <i> with an <svg>: React crashes removing it (removeChild), Vue throws removing it with v-if and leaves the icon, Lit attribute bindings on it go stale.

element.passThrough: every other attribute stays on the element, which is the icon's root (class fd-icon, data-icon, aria-hidden)
element.confirm: attribute names from contract/custom-elements.json: icon (not name) and size; lint-markup reports <fd-icon name>, which draws nothing

staticSvg.class: followed by the <i>'s classes, or empty
staticSvg.size: data-size="{data-size}" when the <i> has data-size, else empty
staticSvg.rest: every other attribute of the <i> except data-icon, data-size and class, in order; an aria-hidden among them replaces the default
staticSvg.rename: change data-icon and href together; Fire's observer also corrects href from data-icon

sprite.clientOnly: fire.js (icons.js) prepends it to <body> when it loads
sprite.serverRendered: <svg id="fd-icon-sprite" hidden aria-hidden="true">…every symbol from ICONS as <symbol id="i-{name}" viewBox="0 0 24 24">{paths}</symbol>…</svg> in the root layout body; Fire then skips its own
sprite.source: import { ICONS } from 'fire-design/fire/js/icons.js' (safe on the server)

registration.rule: import 'fire-design/elements' before the first render, in the browser only; registering twice is a no-op
registration.react: use wrappers/react (fire-design/react registers in the browser only), or import('fire-design/elements') in an effect; never a static import at the top of a client module: Next renders client components on the server too, and elements.js touches HTMLElement and document as it loads

attributes.rule: strings and numbers the manifest lists as attributes

properties.rule: data the manifest lists as properties (.data on fd-chart, .code on fd-code)
properties.react: the wrapper component from wrappers/react ({Name} {name}={{expr}}), or a ref: useEffect(() => { {ref}.current.{name} = {expr}; }, [{expr}])
properties.vue: :{name}="{expr}" once registered; :{name}.prop="{expr}" or .{name}="{expr}" works before registration

server.react: strings, numbers and true become attributes; objects and functions are left out

typing.react: wrappers/react prop types; IntrinsicElements augmentation exported by the wrappers

vueCompilerOptions.rule: vite.config: vue({ template: { compilerOptions: { isCustomElement: (tag) => tag.startsWith('fd-'), whitespace: 'preserve' } } }); app.config.compilerOptions affects only templates compiled at run time

bind.reactWithoutWrapper: useEffect(() => { const el = {ref}.current; el.addEventListener('{event}', {handler}); return () => el.removeEventListener('{event}', {handler}); }, [{handler}])

notWorking.react: on{event}={…} does not compile under SWC (Next: "JSX Namespace is disabled"); {...{ 'on{event}': fn }} works only on custom elements on the client
notWorking.vue: @{event} on a Vue component is a component emit, not a DOM listener (A)

L1.lit: firstUpdated() (or updated()) { init(this); }, without waiting for child elements: fd-chart draws from its properties whenever init ran

L2.when: after an update that inserts or replaces Fire markup (lists, key changes, v-if)
L2.react: useFire's effect runs after every commit (no dependency list)

L3.lit: the router outlet calls init(outlet) after rendering
L3.react: the root layout's client component: useEffect(() => { import('fire-design').then((f) => f.init(document)); }, [usePathname()])

L5.react: Fire running before hydrateRoot makes React rebuild the tree, losing Fire's changes; load Fire inside useEffect

L6.rule: Fire markup lives in light DOM: Fire's listeners are delegated on document and use event.target.closest()
L6.renderEqual: a component's host element inside .fd-page is a node of its own: screens render their own .fd-page with hosts at display: contents, or render-equal runs with --transparent <host selectors> (R12)

L7.rule: no teardown; Fire has no destroy function

L8.when: a route change that moves as one page (0.8; opt in)
L8.lit: transition(() => render the route) from fire-design, awaited by the router's handler
L8.react: data-fd-transition="fade" written once on <html> (N3) and a <ViewTransition> around each screen (React 19.3, Next App Router); no call to transition(); R14 ignores the vt-* attributes
L8.vue: router.beforeResolve opens transition() with an update that lets the navigation go on; afterEach and onError end it

lifecycle.idempotent: init(root) is a no-op for elements it has seen (once, keyed on the element); the forms and texture modules also enhance inserted markup through their own observers

ownership.rule: Write the value the Fire markup shows, never bind these to changing state; change Fire's state through Fire's API, the trigger, or a key remount (O1)
ownership.scope: These are Fire-owned on the elements Fire manages (component roots, triggers, panels, items); aria-label only where the element had none.

filledContainers.fire: replaced with an <svg>
rewrites .fd-secret-value into the masked start and end; a framework text update shows the secret unmasked
innerHTML replaced with highlighted lines
innerHTML replaced with the tree (its JSON script removed)
appends plot, legend and table, or clears all but the JSON script
filledContainers.rule: fd-chart with .data when data changes; static markup when it never changes

filledContainers.fire: appends a canvas or frames, or fills itself when empty
filledContainers.rule: render it empty; fd-texture for ascii fields

filledContainers.fire: removes .fd-diff-src, builds head and body
removes the authored input or textarea, builds boxes, tokens, rows and a hidden carrier
inserts <output> after the input, appends ticks
moves its children into .fd-kv-text, appends a copy button
rewrites text into parameter spans
rebuilt on every init
replaced when the step count changes
builds or rewrites the conversation or rows
re-appends items when filtering; label children replaced with <mark>
appends a jump button; message text replaced with <mark> while filtering
appends or prepends an indicator, thumb or marker
filledContainers.rule: items may change; L2 keeps it right

filledContainers.fire: inserts the check SVG when none
adds anchors and ids, fills empty lists
wrapped or moved
adds the search, the chip list, the Clear button and a live region; sets hidden (and data-fd-hid) on the rows or items of its target and on [data-fd-none]
filledContainers.rule: render every row once as static markup with its data-<field>; to filter your own data use fd:filter and matches()

filledContainers.fire: sets hidden on entries, list, .fd-empty and pager; fills an empty nav.fd-pagination; writes the text of .fd-site-posts-count
filledContainers.rule: render every entry once with an empty nav.fd-pagination; filterPosts() from script

filledContainers.fire: copies the list after itself (aria-hidden, inert) and sets data-cloned
fills the mark, the name or the logo image from data-fd-brand or setBrand(); without a mark it draws the name's initial
filledContainers.rule: render each once with the name as its text; change the brand with setBrand(); the JSON script follows M2

filledContainers.fire: fills .fd-doc-frame-media with an or a placeholder tile and writes data-state
filledContainers.rule: render the figure with data-fd-src, data-fd-alt and an empty media; setPicture(frame, url) changes it

fieldRule.react: defaultValue / defaultChecked; read fd:change or the submitted form (F7)
fieldRule.lit: attribute value for the start; read fd:change

N1.rule: Server components render plain Fire markup; Fire's modules load in the browser only, after hydration: import('fire-design') inside useEffect in a client component

N2.rule: boot.js: a blocking <script src="/fire/boot.js" nonce={nonce} /> in the root layout <head>, served from public/fire/boot.js (copied from node_modules/fire-design/fire/boot.js before build); not next/script

N3.devLogs: Next 16 dev logs attribute hydration mismatches to the browser console, text and structure mismatches only to its overlay and terminal ([browser] lines): a check reads both

N4.rule: suppressHydrationWarning on every server-rendered element with data-fd-vars; a check reads the console and the dev server output (N3)

N5.rule: JSON scripts via dangerouslySetInnerHTML and jsonForScript

N6.rule: import 'fire-design/css' in app/layout.tsx; TypeScript needs declare module 'fire-design/css' (or a types entry for ./css). Turbopack lowers light-dark() too: package.json "browserslist": ["chrome >= 123", "edge >= 123", "firefox >= 120", "safari >= 17.5"]

N7.rule: elements and wrappers/react in client components only; never a static import of fire-design/elements (C1): fire-design/react, or import('fire-design/elements') in an effect

N8.rule: <FireSprite /> in the root layout body (icons.sprite.serverRendered); fire/js/icons.d.ts types fire-design/fire/js/icons.js; @types/react lacks hidden on SVG: augment SVGAttributes with hidden?: boolean

H1.rule: a build step writes themeToCss(record, { selector }) to a .css file loaded after fire.css; expandTheme(record).attributes go on <html>; never a run-time <style> element

H2.rule: <link rel="stylesheet" href="fire/fire.css"><link rel="stylesheet" href="theme.css"> and the attributes on <html>

H3.rule: import 'fire-design/css'; import './fire-theme.css'; in main.ts; attributes on <html> in index.html

H4.rule: the same imports in app/layout.tsx; attributes spread on <html> (N3); the browserslist of N6 keeps light-dark() as written

H5.rule: a look chosen at run time goes through setTheme, setDensity and tweaks.js; boot.js restores it before first paint

P1.rule: works: Vite emits external module scripts and stylesheet links; Fire uses CSSOM setProperty; JSON scripts need no nonce
P1.webkitArtefact: Playwright's WebKit reports every <select> under a strict style-src as a style-src-attr violation (empty sample) with a console error that begins "Refused to apply a stylesheet because its hash, its nonce, or 'unsafe-inline'", even on a bare page; a starter's CSP check may ignore that report, by that exact message only, in WebKit only

P3.rule: nonce per request from proxy.ts (next.proxy); routes become dynamic; development adds 'unsafe-eval' and style-src 'unsafe-inline'

P4.rule: no style, :style, v-show, styleMap, inline handlers, eval, or inline <script> other than application/json

P5.rule: build.cssTarget: ['chrome123', 'edge123', 'firefox120', 'safari17.5'] in vite.config (P1's companion). Vite's default target makes lightningcss lower light-dark() into a theme-only toggle, which breaks color-scheme overrides (a light-only QR figure turns dark). Next.js and Turbopack: a browserslist in package.json (N6)

X1.rule: data-label-<key> (dots in the key become hyphens) on a component, an ancestor or <html>; a plain data-* attribute in every target; read each time Fire writes the label

X2.rule: the data-fd-labels dictionary is in the document before Fire writes its first label; parsed once

B1.notes: positional like the board; a non-list is an error; $index in scope

B6.board: value, checked or selected with a whole hole
B6.react: value={ccText({expr})} with onChange={the board's input handler}, else readOnly; checked={ccTruthy({expr})}; selected on <option> becomes the <select>'s value
B6.confirmedBy: Facet: runtime LIVE_PROPERTIES = value, checked, selected

B7.board: on{event}="{{{handler}}}" (name lowercased; doubleclick → dblclick; onfd:select → fd:select); called with (event, loopLocals)

B8.functions: bound to the parent board's logic; passed as callbacks

B9.all: the Fire markup the component's entry in contract/catalog.json gives (props to the root's data-* attributes), written by the rules above; on-* props are handlers (B7); a <cc-component> from a system with no catalogue mapping makes the board refused for export, naming the component
B9.confirmedBy: Facet: a card's api has props, parts and example, no markup mapping

B10.board: <script type="text/x-cc-board"> class Board extends BoardLogic(props, tweaks) { state; values(); setState(update); mounted() }
B10.lit: a light-DOM LitElement holding logic = new Board(props, tweaks); setState → requestUpdate(); mounted() in firstUpdated
B10.react: useBoard(Board, props, tweaks): the instance in useRef, setState bumps a counter; mounted() in useEffect([])
B10.vue: useBoard with a shallowRef version; mounted() in onMounted

B11.board: the literal initial state object only
B11.all: moved to {Name}.sample.(ts|js) and imported as the starting state; literals computed in values() stay in the view; a non-literal state makes the exporter refuse the board

B12.all: component props with the tweak defaults, except $size (the board's frame size)

B13.all: dropped; a board with its own <cc-head> CSS is refused for export with the reason

renderEqual.R2: Outside <pre> and <textarea>: collapse whitespace runs to one space; whitespace-only text between block or flex children counts as absent.
renderEqual.R3: Attributes compared as a set, names in lowercase, order ignored.
renderEqual.R4: class compared as a set of tokens.
renderEqual.R5: Form state compared through properties (value, checked, selected, open), not attributes or a textarea's text child.
renderEqual.R7: data-fd-vars is removed by Fire; compare the custom properties it set (computed styles).
renderEqual.R8: Ignore #fd-icon-sprite and framework root and wrapper elements.
renderEqual.R9: Generated ids (Fire's core.js id(): fd-<words>-<base-36 counter>; ids that only url(#…) or href="#…" inside the same <svg> reference; framework ids) are renamed in the document order of the elements that carry them, with every reference (for, the aria-* id lists, popovertarget, href="#…", url(#…) in attributes and computed styles): compare the referenced element, not the id string.
renderEqual.R10: SVG geometry (x, y, width, height, cx, cy, r, rx, ry, x1…y2, and the numbers in d, points, transform, viewBox) is equal within 0.5 px.
renderEqual.R11: Margins count only when the two boxes (relative to the root) differ by more than 0.5 px (Chromium can report a stale computed auto margin).
renderEqual.R12: --transparent <selector> (repeatable) treats matching elements as wrappers, inside Fire nodes too (a component's host element).
renderEqual.R13: Capture a settled page: no DOM mutation, no change of the root's box and no pending timeout of 2 s or less for 400 ms, up to the ready timeout; wait only for fd- elements to be defined; the page's CSP is bypassed for the capture (the starters check the policy in their own browser pass).
renderEqual.R14: Ignore React's view-transition bookkeeping attributes (vt-*: vt-name, vt-update, vt-enter, vt-exit, vt-share): <ViewTransition> writes them into the server HTML and adds no element.
renderEqual.R15: The pixel shot is of the root alone: for the shot only, on both sides, every element that is neither the root, inside it, nor one of its ancestors is made visibility:hidden and restored afterwards (layout untouched; the root's own fixed or sticky descendants stay): the comparison is of the root, the shell around it belongs to the product.

W1.rule: data-fd-surface="app|website|phone|email" on <html> or one element is an ordinary data-* attribute with a value (A9); Fire has no script for it; the markup lint reads it (surface-mismatch, a warning) and --surface sets it for files that declare none
W1.react: a static prop on <html> in the root layout, beside suppressHydrationWarning (N3)

W2.rule: nav.fd-tabbar is a direct child of .fd-app with a.fd-tabbar-item (icon and fd-tabbar-label); a More button is button.fd-tabbar-item[data-fd-mobile-nav][aria-controls][aria-expanded=false]; the router link sets aria-current=page, aria-expanded is Fire's (O1)

W3.rule: a screen's states are blocks of markup chosen by the framework from a typed state read from the address (?state=); the template's inline demo script is a specimen and is not exported; fd-states is the Fire form (data-state shows the child with the matching data-when; data-state is Fire's, O1: setState() or a key remount)
W3.lit: the route's PageState selects the template
W3.react: searchParams on the server page selects the blocks
W3.vue: the route's query selects them with v-if

W4.rule: a website section is plain markup: section.fd-site-section.fd-site-<type> with one .fd-site-container inside .fd-site, with ordinary data-* attributes; no element exists for a section; what Fire changes in one is the O2 rows for the listing, the logo strip, .fd-brand and the picture frame, and the sign-up form's data-state (O1), and after hydration it inserts one span[data-fd-site-sentinel] at the start of .fd-site (the header's scrolled state); every img inside .fd-site has alt, width and height (lint: img-attrs); call init(root) after rendering (L1, L2)
